## 固定收益市場主線

聯準會暫停升息，投資人下修12月之後的緊縮預期，卻未放下對通膨的疑慮，美債殖利率曲線因而轉陡。2年期殖利率下降3.94個基點至4.6975%，10年期上升2.08個基點至5.0175%，30年期上升3.23個基點至5.3426%。主席Kevin Warsh承認金融情勢已經收緊，但沒有稱之為緊縮，也不願承諾下一次利率調整方向。這番說法支撐了短天期美債，較長天期債券則仍承受物價壓力持續的風險。

聯準會以10票對2票維持3.75%至4%的目標區間，投下反對票的理事Lisa Cook與克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack均主張升息25個基點。官員將經濟成長的描述由穩健上調為強勁。Warsh並宣布，在每年八次會議不變的安排下，減少利率決策的表決次數，使未來政策調整時點多了一項變數。10年期損益兩平通膨率的升幅超過實質殖利率的降幅，顯示當日曲線轉陡更直接反映通膨疑慮，而非各期限資金成本全面上升。

信用市場則呈現另一種融資約束。Barclays正探詢為逾$100億AI基礎設施債務投保，以騰出進一步放款的空間；最新報導也顯示，愈來愈多資料中心融資必須提供兩位數殖利率才能吸引投資人。然而，美國高收益債整體利差收盤變動不大，硬通貨計價新興市場債利差還明顯收窄。龐大的募資規模與部分風險愈來愈難轉售的情況並存，壓力並不均勻，尚非融資市場全面關閉。

## 聯準會暫停升息，殖利率曲線轉陡

Warsh的說明，讓投資人有理由將下一次可能升息與整輪緊縮的最終幅度分開看待。他強調消費支出健康、企業投資穩健，同時否定經濟開始過熱的說法。通膨是委員會討論的核心；他表示，必須防止能源及相關價格上漲更廣泛地傳導至經濟其他領域。

聲明除了將成長描述上調，也指出國內支出具韌性，就業增加與勞動人口成長同步，失業率則變動不大。官員希望取得更多資訊，再決定何種政策立場足以讓通膨回到2%。這保留了再次升息的可能，但10月按兵不動不等於承諾12月採取行動。

對短天期債券而言，主席如何評估金融情勢尤其重要。他表示，市場參與者配置資本時已更審慎挑選，整體情勢也比先前收緊，但不願稱之為緊縮。投資人因此下修2027年進一步升息的預期，聯邦資金期貨不再完全反映本輪還會升息三次。Bloomberg在決策後的報導指出，12月升息25個基點的機率仍約90%。市場主要調整的是此後還要升多少，而非放棄12月升息的預期。

Nuveen的Tony Rodriguez認為，Warsh的鷹派程度低於原本可能的表現，部分投資人因而更擔憂較長天期債券。BMO Capital Markets的Ian Lyngen則表示，短端反應顯示，市場認為9月升息迄今已發揮效果；依此解讀，若12月再升息，市場認定需要第三次升息的程度可能下降。這些看法比起將目標區間不變一概視為美債利多，更能解釋各期限表現的分歧。

5年期殖利率小幅下降0.70個基點至4.8371%，表現介於漲勢較強的2年期與下跌的較長天期債券之間。2年與10年期利差擴大6.02個基點至32個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大7.17個基點至64.51個基點。雖然當日長端調整較大，整條附息公債殖利率曲線仍低於一週前：2年與10年期分別下降10.85與10.15個基點，30年期降幅則較小，為6.63個基點。

10年期當日殖利率上升，來自通膨補償增加。TIPS實質殖利率下降1.01個基點至2.6315%，損益兩平通膨率則上升3.09個基點至2.386%。過去一個月，實質殖利率下降19.25個基點，損益兩平通膨率上升4.70個基點，使名目殖利率合計下降14.55個基點。週三延續了實質殖利率下滑、通膨補償走高的分歧，卻中斷了近期長天期名目殖利率下降的走勢。

Warsh調整會議安排，另為政策時點帶來變數。FOMC每年仍將召開八次會議，但2027年其中一次將專門討論整體貨幣策略，不進行利率表決，也不發布聲明；2028年則有兩次會議保留給廣泛討論，而非決定利率。減少的是作成利率決策的場合，不是委員會開會的次數。

Neuberger Berman的Robert Dishner表示，投資人正據此重新評估明年的升息路徑。TD Securities的Gennadiy Goldberg則強調應事先告知市場，因為已有合約依既定會議日期交易。依Warsh的構想，減少利率決策可讓兩次表決之間累積更多資訊，但也可能使市場對剩餘決策日期更加敏感。策略會議與利率決策會議的具體配置，將決定新安排如何反映在市場定價中。

週三美國數據顯示，房貸需求有所改善，貿易對經濟成長的貢獻卻較不利。截至10月23日當週，MBA房貸申請增加3.4%，扭轉前週下滑5.3%的走勢，30年期房貸利率也由7.41%略降至7.37%。整體市場指數由188.6升至195.0，再融資指數由503.1升至516.8，購屋指數由129.2升至134.1。兩類活動均改善，但借款利率仍超過7%。

9月商品貿易逆差初值由修正後的$1,320.7億擴大至$1,349億，未如市場共識預期縮小至$1,300億。批發庫存月增0.6%，高於預期與前期的0.5%；不含汽車的零售庫存月增0.4%，前期則修正為增加0.1%。亞特蘭大聯準銀行的第三季GDPNow模型估值由3.4%略降至3.3%，政府估值則尚待公布。

能源繼續增加通膨展望的複雜度。WTI收漲2.16%至每桶$102.06，Brent上漲0.27%至$114.19，後者仍較一個月前高17.19%。EIA公布，截至10月23日當週原油庫存減少189.2萬桶，市場原預期持平，前週則減少306.1萬桶。餾分油庫存減少146.2萬桶，超過預期的90萬桶；汽油庫存卻增加387萬桶，與預期減少90萬桶相反。各項油品庫存走勢不一，並非所有燃料都同時短缺。

當日油市疑慮也包括《華爾街日報》的報導：華府已警告波斯灣國家，準備因應美國期中選舉後可能對伊朗重新發動短暫而猛烈的攻擊，但川普尚未決定是否進行。以色列選舉的詳細計票也未定局；完成近93%計票時，內唐亞胡聯盟預估取得53席、Eisenkot陣營48席、阿拉伯政黨19席，均未達單獨過半所需的61席。票數仍在變動，加上籌組聯合政府的協商，使衝突下一階段的政治走向仍不明朗。

股市在正常交易時段上漲，S&P 500漲0.28%至7,743.98點，Nasdaq 100漲0.55%，半導體類股上漲1.75%；美元指數下跌0.16%至102.155。Oracle預測2029會計年度自由現金流將達$300億，投資人原本預期該年度為負值，帶動股價上漲11%。股市走強與美債曲線轉陡、通膨補償上升同時發生，並未取代後兩者所反映的訊息。

## AI借款擴張，風險轉售遇到瓶頸

最新融資報導將AI信用市場的焦點，從能否安排龐大融資承諾，轉向貸款機構能否將風險移出資產負債表。據知情人士透露，Barclays已向保險業者探詢，為逾$100億AI基礎設施貸款取得違約保障，部分融資希望承保超過50%的信用風險。洽談仍在探索階段，最終規模與時程均未決定。

這類保險可釋出監管資本，讓銀行承作更多貸款，但前提是保險業者願意承接風險。Willis Towers Watson在5月發布的調查發現，部分非貿易信用風險保險業者對資料中心的曝險已接近產業上限，甚至額度已滿。另一家歐洲大型銀行的資深科技業放款主管向Bloomberg表示，出售債務或移轉風險可能耗時五個月，拖慢資本回收並投入新專案的速度。

問題不只是找到高評等企業為交易提供支持。Citadel Securities分析師Tucker Roberts指出，買家還必須願意繼續承接由同一小群科技公司支持的曝險。這些企業本身要籌資支應投資計畫，同時又透過保證、長期合約，以及專案出問題時可能出手相助的市場預期，累積更多風險。Citadel並未預測信用緊縮即將到來，擔心的是產業融資企圖與投資人承接集中風險意願之間的差距愈來愈大。

Bloomberg報導，目前至少18筆資料中心高收益債與槓桿貸款融資的殖利率達兩位數。JPMorgan與Goldman Sachs必須提高Volta Infrastructure Holdings一筆$50億聯貸的利息支付並加大發行折價，使殖利率超過11%。Morgan Stanley的ABS策略師Carolyn Campbell指出，最高評等資料中心債券的殖利率，已由2026年初不到5%升至接近7%；對租金收入鎖定於長約的設施而言，借款成本接近8%時，發債難度會顯著提高。

整體融資成本的上升，與合約所訂信用利差是不同層面的問題。開發商的籌資成本增加，固定租金收入卻不會自動跟著調高。Campbell估計，今年資料中心在ABS與CMBS市場的發行額約$220億，在建設需求擴大之際，僅勉強跟上去年規模。影響哪些專案能推進的，不只是已宣布的支出金額，也包括市場可提供何種資本結構。

合約的退出條款同樣受到更嚴格檢視。一家避險基金發現，若完工延誤超過三個月，客戶即可退出，因而拒絕參與一筆交易；參與其他專案的律師，也見過延誤180天或更久便可終止合約的條款。兩者門檻不同，卻都可能使放款人在仍須支應建設資產融資時，失去預期的客戶現金流。Oracle上月發出不可抗力通知，尋求在新墨西哥州專案延誤時遞延付款，也加深了市場對這些條款的關注。

重新定價不只發生在專案貸款，也出現在企業信用保險。據Bloomberg報導，Oracle、SpaceX、Nvidia與Meta的信用保障成本上週升至紀錄高點。Bloomberg投資級科技債指數的平均殖利率約6%，較一年前高約1.4個百分點。這些價格反映市場認定的信用風險與融資壓力增加，但各發行人的債務義務，以及對個別專案承諾的支持，仍有重大差異。

借款總量卻持續擴大。全球政府、金融機構與企業的投資級及非投資級債券銷售額已達$6.61兆，較去年同期增加15%，且超過2025年全年紀錄。其中，雲端運算公司與資料中心開發商發債近$3,680億，超過去年同期六倍，占整體增額約三分之一。這些債券銷售數字並未涵蓋AI籌資所用的全部貸款、租賃與股權資金。

Amazon在全球發行人中排名第四，僅次於德國、歐盟與義大利；德國與義大利的合計數字包括政府支持的借款人。Amazon也是最大的企業借款人，其次為Alphabet。美國十大企業發行人中，有五家是科技公司。Bloomberg Intelligence預估，其追蹤的一組超大規模雲端業者與新興雲端業者，未來三年投資額將接近$4.5兆，意味當前風險轉售的難題，面對的仍是持續存在的未來融資需求。

市場對這些困難有多少屬於短期現象，看法並不一致。RBC Global Asset Management的Neil Sun認為，短期供給確有消化不良，但強勁的運算需求將支撐投資延續至2027年。美國財政部長Scott Bessent在聯準會決策後表示，融資仍在完成，也可透過股權籌資。他認為新興雲端業者只占整體生態系的一小部分，不覺得這些壓力構成問題；這與放款人對風險集中及曝險移轉耗時的擔憂形成對照。

固定收益市場收盤前，企業營運表現提供了方向不一的訊息。Microsoft在盤後公布的雲端營收優於預期，Alphabet的營收與獲利則低於預估，兩者股價在延長交易時段走勢分歧。Oracle的長期現金流預測，稍早已提振正常交易時段的市場情緒。這組結果既不是全面否定AI支出，也不能顯示每項龐大投資計畫都已帶來預期報酬。

紐約時間下午5時50分、固定收益市場收盤後，Bloomberg另報導一筆德州資料中心融資轉售的具體延誤。以Morgan Stanley為首的銀行，原希望在9月出售$50億至$70億高收益債，為Hubbard的Nexus專案約$150億建設融資中的一部分再融資。該專案租予Anthropic，並由Google提供支持。德州為檢視電網而暫停新專案，導致發債延後，目前可能改在未來一年分批出售。

這套融資包括$142億一年期貸款與$14億五年期循環額度，其中過橋貸款已撥款，銀行承擔的是已動用曝險，不只是尚未動用的承諾。Citi、Intesa Sanpaolo、Mizuho、Morgan Stanley、MUFG、Royal Bank of Canada與Santander共同安排融資，每家承諾約$20億；包括Santander在內的部分銀行正尋求更多參貸機構。發債延後拉長了銀行持有風險的時間，也使州政府的審查直接影響原定再融資時程。

## 借款人壓力反映在債券價格與債權條款

Dave & Buster's聘請Moelis協助處理$15億債務，與PJT Partners及Gibson Dunn合作的債權人團體則已簽署合作協議，並爭取更多債權人加入。在重整可能使債權人分裂為不同陣營之際，這項協議旨在擴大放款人之間的協調，目前尚未公布重整條款。

這家遊樂餐飲業者一筆2029年到期、規模$6.91億的定期貸款，週三報價為面額的55.875%，低於2月17日的93.75%。其債務由定期貸款與循環融資組成。第二季同店銷售年減2.9%，調整後盈餘由$1.298億降至$9,890萬。Moody's在9月維持B3企業評等，但因利息保障能力偏弱、槓桿偏高及營運低迷，將展望改為負向。聘請顧問是公司對這些惡化情況採取的新措施。

Aston Martin第三季營運雖改善，仍未阻止債務進一步增加。受惠銷售組合轉向較昂貴車款，營收成長36%至£3.89億，稅前虧損縮小至£7,700萬；管理階層維持財測，並表示減緩現金消耗已有進展。但淨負債仍升至£15.7億，債券週三約報面額的47%，低於10月初的約55%。

這項部位拖累Arini Capital Management，其旗艦基金10月截至23日虧損12%，今年累計虧損約26%；該基金7月底管理資產為$75億。知悉交易情況的人士表示，創辦人Hamza Lemssouguer正以更防禦的方式管理既有部位，承接更多債券的出價也較不積極。其他投資人同樣愈來愈不願買入Arini持有大量部位的較弱信用債券。

個別證券已呈現這種相互影響。Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection一筆2028年到期、規模$3億的債券，由9月底面額的92%以上跌至75%以下。Bloomberg歐洲CCC級債券指數截至9月已連續四個月虧損，10月更可能成為四年來表現最差的月份。另一家業者Sona Asset Management的主要避險基金，10月上半月也下跌3.1%。這些損失使部分傳統買家不再那麼願意承接最弱債券、緩和賣壓。

不過，Arini仍有新資金流入。其信用策略已募得$15億，並重新開放既有投資人申購；其中逾$4億已於10月初配置，其餘預計至2月陸續投入。因此，現階段買盤較不積極，與沒有後續資金是兩回事。Arini持有Aston Martin債務之際，債權人也正就車廠先前取得的£5.5億HPS融資提起訴訟；週三的新進展是季度業績與債券價格，而非該爭議獲得新的解決。

Trans-Oil因延後揭露財報，遭遇更劇烈的即時價格反應。這家摩爾多瓦穀物出口商表示，截至6月30日年度的經查核財報，最遲將於11月27日公布，理由是需要更多時間完成查核程序。其$4.5億、2029年11月到期債券隨後最多下跌7.4個面額百分點，至面額的58%。公司計畫10月30日公布第一季營運成果，並稱儘管物流困難、區域供應令人擔憂，初步估算仍令人鼓舞。7月取得逾$2.45億承諾及延長借款基礎融資額度，與原訂本月進行的再融資及擴大額度，仍是不同事項。

貸款文件研究則更廣泛地說明，為何債權人愈來愈重視法律保障。週三引用的JPMorgan數據顯示，美國槓桿貸款中，價格高於面額的比重降至9.8%，為17個月低點。Barclays的Corry Short一項新研究發現，較強的債權保障條款可改善新貸款的發行定價，但也質疑，出資方以作風激進著稱，這項聲譽本身對定價究竟有多大影響。當保護性條款薄弱，債務管理交易可能在企業最終償債能力尚未確定前，就改變不同放款人的回收情況；此時條款與聲譽的區別格外重要。

小型卡車運輸業者則提供另一項新近報導的財務壓力指標。Bloomberg統計，今年已有221家卡車運輸公司破產。Truckstop與Bloomberg Intelligence過去兩個月進行的調查發現，約三分之二小型業者的營收較一年前持平或下降，近40%預期六個月後已退出卡車運輸業，或對未來沒有把握。受訪者一般經營不超過20輛牽引車，並非針對最大型上市運輸業者的調查。

這群業者同時承受柴油、保險費用，以及設備債務、浮動利率借款、應收帳款承購融資與商戶現金墊款的壓力。Stoneman Trucking在5月聲請破產保護後，業主已放棄繼續經營，正走向第7章清算。設備負債較少的大型業者較能吸收成本；Triumph Financial的Aaron Graft表示，沒有設備債務、且安全紀錄合格的業者表現良好。調查所指出的是特定借款人群體的壓力，而非所有貨運公司的共同財務處境。

部分企業仍有其他融資選擇。Lionsgate正透過MUFG與投資人討論，可能以片庫作為擔保發債。據Bloomberg Intelligence，其片庫擁有逾20,000部電影與電視節目，每年帶來約$10億收入。公司6月30日的企業債務逾$19億，包括一筆超過$10億、2030年9月到期、與智慧財產權連結的貸款；該貸款利率為SOFR加225個基點，每季償還當時未償本金的2.5%。BI的Geetha Ranganathan表示，證券化可能降低籌資成本，但也會降低公司在潛在收購案中運用片庫的彈性。洽談仍在初期，尚未訂定發行條件。

## 主權融資的關鍵在買家與期限

一項針對美國財政部與國務院資料的新分析顯示，2026年前八個月美國融資來源出現明顯變化。被歸類為最親近華府的國家與地區，淨買入不含國庫券的美國公債$1,743億，較一年前減少逾60%，為2021年以來同期最低。日本僅買入$3.89億，減少99%；南韓則賣出$238億，為1977年有紀錄以來同期最多，台灣也是淨賣方。

分析涵蓋57個國家與地區的官方及民間投資人，依其在聯合國重要決議案上與美國的投票一致程度分組，買入數字則涵蓋原始發行期限超過一年的證券。保管地歸屬可能將持有部位記在金融中心，而非最終持有人所在地。因此，數字呈現的是已記錄需求的變化，不能歸結為各國政府共同指導出售美債的單一政策。

亞洲貨幣疲弱、本國市場殖利率更具吸引力，以及更偏好股票與存款，都是可能的原因。美國外交關係協會研究員Brad Setser指出，外國資產愈來愈多由央行外匯存底以外的機構持有，包括退休基金與國有銀行。這可能使官方美債需求下降，卻仍有可觀的美元資產需求存在於其他機構。

8月外國持有美債仍達$7.85兆，接近紀錄高點，但持有比重已由2012年的52%降至不到三分之一。銀行、共同基金與避險基金等民間投資人，持有聯邦債務的比重則升至約70%，接近1990年以來最高。State Street的Masahiko Loo與Deutsche Bank的Shoki Omori認為，這意味美國更依賴對價格敏感的買家。這是1月至8月融資結構的發現，不是週三資金流向的衡量。

英國則展現調整發債期限組合的即時效果。財政大臣John Healey公布預算，債務管理局（DMO）並將較長天期債券的計畫供給由£224億降至£155億後，英國公債上漲。DMO提高對國庫券的依賴，並確認自2027年1月起，以標售方式發行12個月期國庫券。市場反應期間，10年期英國公債殖利率一度下降4個基點至5.30%。

預算責任署（OBR）確認，2029至2030財政年度仍有£150億財政餘裕。投資人歡迎預算沒有大規模長期讓利措施，且在赤字下降的同時，債務占GDP比率走勢大致持平。截至倫敦下午3時，10年期殖利率全日波動區間僅7個基點，低於Rachel Reeves在2024年首度公布預算當日的22個基點，以及2022年迷你預算期間的40個基點。實際借款計畫，為先前長天期發行將減少的預期提供了具體內容。

中國面對的則是大量供給與低殖利率並存。中誠信國際信用評級與興業證券估計，11月及12月中央與地方政府債券淨發行額至少人民幣2.2兆元，為這兩個月份歷來第二高，僅次於2024年。截至10月23日，淨融資已達人民幣11.15兆元。10年期殖利率約1.62%，接近紀錄低點；中國人民銀行週三則連續第六個交易日淨投放流動性。

在消費、就業與基礎設施投資疲弱之際，預期發債旨在支撐經濟活動。中誠信的袁海霞預期，更強的財政支持將縮小基建投資的降幅，並預計央行以公開市場操作平抑發債帶來的流動性波動。興業證券認為，11月可能是供給高峰，但警告隨政策與經濟情況變化，實際發行可能與計畫有明顯差距。預測中的融資，仍不同於已經支出的資金。

日本最新的基金經理人訪談，則顯示市場對較長天期公債更為正面。T. Rowe Price偏好長天期債券，Allianz Global Investors正選擇性增持中長天期債券，BNP Paribas Asset Management則已增加20年與30年期部位。30年期殖利率較10月稍早的4.25%高點已下降近40個基點，2年與30年期利差自7月以來收窄約70個基點。壽險業已連續四個月淨買入超長天期日本公債，外國投資人也連續三個月淨買入。

這些買家認為，需求回升與日本央行進一步緊縮，可能有助壓低期限溢價，但信心仍取決於財政資金來源。Brandywine的Carol Lye因等待可信的籌資計畫，尚未買回今年稍早賣出的30年期部位。T. Rowe Price的Vincent Chung與Deutsche Securities的Omori也警告，若支出沒有相應財源，或發債計畫未能減少超長天期供給，近期曲線趨平走勢可能反轉。

日本企業信用走勢卻不同。美國收盤後發布的報導顯示，10月1日至28日，Bloomberg追蹤的40家日本主要企業，5年期CDS全部上升，增幅中位數為12個基點，是2022年9月以來最大惡化幅度；SoftBank與Nissan的利差擴大最多。本土公司債利差約在兩年半高點。Nomura的Kazuma Ogino認為，壓力來自大量供給與政府公債殖利率下降，也包括對AI投資及法國公共財政的疑慮。主權債需求回升，並未讓企業借款人獲得同樣有利的定價。

## 能源成本傳導，各國央行選擇分歧

加拿大將隔夜利率上調至2.5%，為逾三年來首次升息，目的是降低能源價格持續高漲帶動其他商品與服務漲價的風險。這項決定符合市場與Bloomberg經濟學家共識。總裁Tiff Macklem表示，可能仍須進一步緊縮，但不確定性意味應審慎前進，逐次會議決定。

央行大幅調整預測，將2027年平均通膨由2%上修至3.1%，回到2%目標的時間也延至2028年中。2026年成長預測由0.7%升至1%，2027及2028年則均由1.8%升至2%。Macklem表示，目前能源成本的傳導有限，但隨成本在經濟中擴散，預期明年非能源通膨將上升。

理事會也曾考慮按兵不動，因為能源仍占通膨升幅的大部分，經濟仍有閒置產能，且與美國的關稅爭端威脅成長。就業已連續兩個月下降，房市也疲弱。決策公布後，加幣在每美元兌C$1.4046附近變動不大，2年期殖利率則在當日區間內小幅下滑。預期中的升息，並未引起同樣強烈的市場重新定價。

住房市場凸顯，以升息對抗輸入性衝擊的國內代價。央行目前預測，住宅房地產至2028年對經濟成長幾乎沒有貢獻。資深副總裁Carolyn Rogers表示，升息會加重既有抑制。Desjardins分析師Royce Mendes與Tiago Figueiredo估計，未來幾個月部分浮動利率借款人在續約時，還款額將面臨約50%的跳升，但也指出房貸拖欠率仍低於歷史水準。相較長期固定利率架構，頻繁續約與普遍使用浮動利率借款，會讓貨幣緊縮更快傳到家庭。

Macklem在另一場訪談中指出，美國龐大赤字與AI借款可能推高全球長期殖利率，並可能提高加拿大的中性利率。不過，他未調整央行目前2.25%至3.25%的中性利率估計，該估計每年4月檢討。他也否認新的Prima預測模型本身導致週三升息。模型整合各產業成本，政策關切的仍是整體通膨未來走勢。

紐西蘭面對顯著通膨風險，卻選擇等待。紐西蘭央行以4票對3票維持官方現金利率2.75%，出乎25位受訪經濟學家中23位預期升息25個基點的判斷。Paul Conway、Hayley Gourley與Karen Silk主張升息；支持維持利率的多數派中，總裁Anna Breman與委員Prasanna Gai相當重視全球情勢可能突然轉變、進而影響需求的風險。

委員會表示，視展望而定，可能需要收緊政策。第三季通膨雖已降至3.7%，央行仍預估第四季在燃料成本與匯率走弱推動下升至4.4%。經濟學家預期，通膨將高於1%至3%目標區間，直到2027年底前後。家庭支出低迷限制部分企業轉嫁成本的能力，但長期通膨也可能影響預期與薪資設定。意外按兵不動後，紐元立即一度下跌1.7%至55.86美分。

泰國連續第四次會議維持附買回利率1%，出席的六名委員全數支持，另一名委員缺席。央行因AI相關出口與投資，將今年與2027年成長預測，分別由2.3%及1.8%上修至2.4%及2.1%；核心通膨預測則由1.5%及1.4%，下修至1.2%及1.3%。9月出口年增24%，但觀光、高負債家庭及脆弱勞動市場，使改善範圍受限。

助理總裁Don Nakornthab表示，若復甦持續，就可減少寬鬆、重建政策空間，同時保留遭遇經濟衝擊時降息的餘地。聲明也警告，利率過低維持太久會帶來金融穩定風險。Pantheon Macroeconomics的Miguel Chanco認為，本次語氣偏中性，不同於8月的鴿派立場。經濟學家對最終將走向政策正常化，還是重新寬鬆仍有分歧，反映泰國需求復甦遠不如美國一致。

澳洲方面，最新變化是對未來決策的預測調整。Commonwealth Bank經濟學家Belinda Allen目前預期，澳洲央行將於11月升息至4.85%。她指出，9月當季通膨過高、官員談話更偏鷹派，且疲弱生產力與強勁的全球資本支出相互作用。她主張的預防性升息，旨在因應海外能源成本及國內產能壓力帶來的上行風險；在加拿大立即行動與紐西蘭意外等待之間，這是另一種政策取向。

## 後續市場焦點

週四12:30 UTC公布的美國成長與通膨數據，將是聯準會暫停升息後首輪重要數據考驗。第三季GDP市場共識為年化成長3.2%，前期為2.2%，亞特蘭大聯準銀行最新模型估值則為3.3%。9月核心PCE預期月增0.3%、年增3.1%，均高於前期的0.2%與3%；整體PCE預期月增0.5%、年增3.6%，前期分別為0.3%與3.4%。在官員仍稱經濟成長強勁之際，這些組合將有助判斷，市場能否維持較小幅度的整輪緊縮預期。

同一時間也將公布個人支出與所得，預期分別增加0.6%及0.3%，前期為0.9%及0.2%。截至10月24日當週初領失業救濟金人數共識為19.9萬人，前週為19.4萬人；續領預估172萬人，前期為172.8萬人。第三季GDP物價指數預期由6.1%降至3.2%，季度核心PCE物價漲幅由3.3%降至2.4%。季度價格指標與9月月度數據涵蓋期間不同，因此可能同時出現整季漲勢放緩、最後一個月卻較強的情況。

日本週四的2年期公債標售與週五的央行決策，將檢驗政府債券需求的回升。市場普遍預期本次維持利率，因此總裁植田和男對後續緊縮與政策利率最終高點的指引，對較長天期債券尤其重要。對新進長端買家而言，更關鍵的是可信的2027財政年度籌資計畫，包括擬議的食品稅減免與國防支出如何取得財源。供給計畫若不符預期，可能打斷近期曲線趨平的走勢。

美國期中選舉選票上，至少有$840億州及地方政府債券提案；依Bloomberg對大型公投的比較，高於2024年的約$810億與去年的$160億。加州占約$600億，德州約$100億。加州最大兩項措施，分別尋求授權$250億收益債以協助購屋，以及$112.5億一般責任債以支持可負擔住宅。這些仍是交由選民授權的請求，投票結果將影響住宅與基礎設施的潛在融資供給，而非既定發債時程。

AI信用方面，德州電網審查左右Hubbard延後的債券再融資，Barclays的保險洽談則取決於交易對手願不願承接更多曝險。兩項各自尚未解決的條件，直接影響銀行資本回收再運用的速度。公開市場上，Microsoft與Alphabet業績分歧，使投資人能將最新營運結果與持續的融資需求對照，而非將運算需求視為整個產業共同而一致的假設。

Trans-Oil將於10月30日公布營運成果，經查核年度財報則最遲11月27日發布，都是債券重挫後的近期揭露焦點。兩份報告涵蓋不同期間，可讓債權人評估公司所稱的復甦與財務狀況。美國休閒業信用方面，在安全事故與債券價格低迷之後，Six Flags的11月5日業績將帶來管理階層下一次更新；CBRE的Colin Mansfield認為，要更公允評估營運走勢，仍須等待明年初的季票資訊。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The Federal Reserve's pause steepened the Treasury curve as investors reduced expectations for tightening beyond December without shedding their concern about inflation. Two-year yields fell 3.94 basis points to 4.6975%, while the 10-year rose 2.08 basis points to 5.0175% and the 30-year increased 3.23 basis points to 5.3426%. Chair Kevin Warsh acknowledged that financial conditions had tightened, but stopped short of describing them as tight. His refusal to commit to the next rate move left short debt supported and longer maturities exposed to persistent price pressure.

The 10-2 decision to maintain the 3.75%-4% target range came with dissents from Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, both seeking a quarter-point increase. Officials upgraded their description of growth to strong from solid. Warsh also announced fewer rate-setting votes within an unchanged eight-meeting annual calendar, adding a new uncertainty to the timing of future policy adjustments. At 10 years, rising inflation compensation more than offset a decline in real yields, giving the day's steepening a clearer inflation dimension than a uniform increase in the cost of money.

Credit markets supplied a separate test of how much financing restraint was already occurring. Barclays was exploring insurance on more than $10 billion of AI infrastructure debt to create room for further lending, while new reporting showed investors demanding double-digit yields on a growing group of data-center financings. Broad U.S. high-yield spreads nevertheless finished little changed, and hard-currency emerging-market spreads tightened noticeably. The pressure remained uneven: enormous capital-raising volumes coexisted with increasingly difficult distribution of particular risks, rather than a general closure of funding markets.

## A Fed Pause Steepens the Curve

Warsh's explanation gave investors grounds to distinguish the next likely increase from the eventual extent of tightening. He emphasized healthy consumer spending and solid business investment while dismissing the suggestion that the economy was beginning to overheat. Inflation dominated the committee's deliberations. Higher energy and related prices, he said, had to be prevented from spreading more widely through the economy.

The statement paired its stronger growth language with resilient domestic spending, job gains keeping pace with the workforce and an unemployment rate that had changed little. Officials wanted additional information before deciding the policy stance needed to return inflation to 2%. That preserved the prospect of another increase without making the October hold a promise to move in December.

The chair's financial-conditions assessment was particularly important for the front end. He said market participants had become more discriminating in allocating capital and that overall conditions were tighter, while declining to call them tight. Investors consequently trimmed expectations for additional increases in 2027, and federal funds futures no longer fully priced three further hikes in the cycle. Bloomberg's post-decision account put the probability of a December quarter-point increase around 90%. The repricing concerned how much would follow, more than the abandonment of December tightening.

Nuveen's Tony Rodriguez judged Warsh less hawkish than he might have been, leaving some investors more concerned about longer debt. BMO Capital Markets' Ian Lyngen said the short-end response suggested the market saw September's increase as effective so far; in that interpretation, a subsequent December move could reduce the perceived need for a third increase. Those assessments explain the divergent maturity performance more directly than treating the unchanged target range as uniformly supportive of Treasuries.

Five-year yields edged down 0.70 basis point to 4.8371%, between the stronger two-year rally and losses farther out. The two- to 10-year spread widened 6.02 basis points to 32 basis points, while the two- to 30-year gap increased 7.17 basis points to 64.51 basis points. The long end bore the larger adjustment even though the entire coupon curve remained below its week-earlier levels. Two- and 10-year yields were down 10.85 and 10.15 basis points over that period; the 30-year decline was a smaller 6.63 basis points.

Inflation compensation accounted for the daily increase at 10 years. The TIPS real yield declined 1.01 basis points to 2.6315%, while the breakeven rose 3.09 basis points to 2.386%. Over the month, the real yield was down 19.25 basis points and the breakeven up 4.70 basis points, leaving the nominal yield 14.55 basis points lower. Wednesday therefore extended the separation between falling real yields and firmer inflation compensation, even as it interrupted the recent decline in nominal long yields.

Warsh's calendar changes added a distinct policy-timing issue. The FOMC will continue to meet eight times annually, but one meeting in 2027 will be devoted to broad monetary strategy, without a rate vote or statement. In 2028, two meetings will be reserved for broad discussion rather than rate setting. The change is thus in the number of decision occasions, not the number of committee gatherings.

Neuberger Berman's Robert Dishner said investors were reassessing next year's hiking path in light of that arrangement. TD Securities' Gennadiy Goldberg emphasized the need for advance notice because contracts already trade against scheduled meetings. Fewer rate decisions may leave more information between votes, as Warsh intends, while concentrating market sensitivity around the remaining decision dates. The detailed allocation of strategy and rate-setting meetings will determine how that adjustment enters pricing.

Wednesday's U.S. releases showed some improvement in mortgage demand alongside a less favorable trade contribution. MBA mortgage applications rose 3.4% in the week ended October 23, reversing the previous 5.3% decline as the 30-year mortgage rate slipped to 7.37% from 7.41%. The overall market index increased to 195.0 from 188.6; refinancing rose to 516.8 from 503.1, and purchases to 134.1 from 129.2. Both activities improved, though at borrowing rates still above 7%.

The advance September goods deficit widened to $134.9 billion from a revised $132.07 billion, rather than narrowing to the $130 billion consensus. Wholesale inventories rose 0.6% on the month, above the 0.5% expectation and previous increase. Retail inventories excluding autos increased 0.4%, following a revised 0.1% gain. The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow estimate for Q3 eased to 3.3% from 3.4%, keeping a model-based growth reading distinct from the government estimate still ahead.

Energy continued to complicate the inflation outlook. WTI finished up 2.16% at $102.06 a barrel, while Brent rose 0.27% to $114.19. Brent remained 17.19% above its month-earlier level. The EIA reported a 1.892 million-barrel crude-stock draw for the week ended October 23, against expectations for no change and a previous 3.061 million-barrel decline. Distillates fell 1.462 million barrels, exceeding the expected 0.9 million-barrel draw, whereas gasoline stocks rose 3.87 million barrels against an expected 0.9 million-barrel decline. The product detail was mixed rather than a common inventory shortage across fuels.

The day's oil concerns included a Wall Street Journal report that Washington had warned Gulf countries to prepare for a possible short, intense renewal of attacks on Iran after the U.S. midterms. Trump had not decided to proceed. Israel's election remained unsettled in the detailed count: with almost 93% tallied, Netanyahu's alliance was projected at 53 seats, Eisenkot's at 48 and Arab parties at 19, against 61 needed for a majority. The changing count and coalition negotiations left the political route to the next phase of the conflict unresolved.

Equities rose through the regular session, with the S&P 500 up 0.28% at 7,743.98 and the Nasdaq 100 gaining 0.55%. Semiconductor shares advanced 1.75%, while the Dollar Index declined 0.16% to 102.155. Oracle's 11% stock gain followed its forecast of $30 billion in fiscal 2029 free cash flow, a period for which investors had expected a negative result. The stronger equity session sat alongside, rather than displaced, the steeper Treasury curve and higher inflation compensation.

## AI Borrowing Meets Distribution Limits

New financing reporting shifted the AI credit discussion from the ability to arrange large commitments toward the ability to move them off lenders' balance sheets. Barclays has been sounding out insurers about default protection on more than $10 billion of AI infrastructure loans. It is seeking cover for more than 50% of the credit risk on some facilities, according to people familiar with the discussions. Talks are exploratory, with final size and timing undecided.

Risk insurance can release regulatory capital and allow banks to undertake additional lending. Its usefulness depends on insurers accepting the exposure, however. A Willis Towers Watson survey released in May found some non-trade credit-risk insurers approaching sector limits or already full on data centers. A senior technology lender at another large European bank told Bloomberg that selling debt or transferring its risk could take five months, slowing the recycling of capital into new projects.

The constraint is not simply finding a highly rated company to support a transaction. Citadel Securities analyst Tucker Roberts argued that buyers must also be willing to absorb additional exposure backed by the same small group of technology companies. Those firms can accumulate risk through guarantees, long-term contracts and expectations of intervention if projects falter, while simultaneously financing their own investment programs. Citadel was not forecasting an imminent credit crunch; its concern was the growing distance between the industry's funding ambitions and investors' willingness to take the resulting concentrations.

At least 18 data-center financings across high-yield bonds and leveraged loans now carry double-digit yields, Bloomberg reported. JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs had to increase interest payments and discounts on Volta Infrastructure Holdings' $5 billion syndicated loan, taking its yield above 11%. Morgan Stanley ABS strategist Carolyn Campbell said the highest-rated data-center bonds had moved from yields below 5% at the start of 2026 to nearer 7%. At borrowing costs approaching 8%, she said, issuance becomes substantially harder for facilities with rental income locked into long leases.

That increase in all-in financing costs matters separately from any contractual credit margin. A fixed rental stream does not rise automatically when a developer's funding becomes more expensive. Campbell put data-center issuance in ABS and CMBS markets at roughly $22 billion this year, barely keeping pace with last year even as the construction requirement expanded. The structure of the available capital, not only the amount of announced spending, is influencing which projects can advance.

Contractual escape clauses are also receiving greater scrutiny. One hedge fund declined a deal after finding that its customer could withdraw if completion was delayed more than three months. Lawyers working on other projects have seen termination rights after delays of 180 days or more. These are different contractual thresholds, but both expose lenders to a loss of expected customer cash flow while they still have a construction asset to finance. Oracle's force-majeure notice last month, seeking to defer payments if a New Mexico project were delayed, has intensified attention to such provisions.

The repricing is visible in corporate credit insurance as well as project loans. Protection costs for Oracle, SpaceX, Nvidia and Meta reached records last week, according to Bloomberg's account. The average yield in the Bloomberg Investment Grade Technology Index was around 6%, about 1.4 percentage points above a year earlier. These prices reflect greater perceived credit risk and financing pressure; the underlying issuers' obligations and the support promised to particular projects still differ materially.

The scale of borrowing nevertheless continues to grow. Global investment-grade and junk-bond sales by governments, financial firms and companies reached $6.61 trillion, 15% above the same point last year and already beyond the 2025 full-year record. Within that total, cloud-computing companies and data-center developers sold almost $368 billion, more than six times the year-earlier amount and about a third of the overall increase. That bond-sales universe is narrower than the full range of loans, leases and equity being raised for AI.

Amazon ranked fourth among issuers globally, behind Germany, the European Union and Italy, with the German and Italian totals including government-backed borrowers. It was the largest corporate borrower, followed by Alphabet. Five of the 10 biggest U.S. corporate issuers were technology firms. Bloomberg Intelligence expects a group of hyperscalers and neoclouds it follows to invest almost $4.5 trillion over the next three years, putting the current distribution problem against a continuing prospective financing requirement.

There is disagreement over how much of the difficulty is temporary. RBC Global Asset Management's Neil Sun described short-term supply indigestion but saw strong demand for computing capacity sustaining investment into 2027. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, speaking after the Fed decision, said financing was still being completed and pointed to equity as another route. He considered neoclouds a small part of the broader ecosystem and did not regard the strains as problematic. His assessment contrasted with lenders' concerns about concentration and the time needed to transfer exposure.

Operating results offered contrasting evidence before the fixed-income close. Microsoft exceeded cloud-revenue expectations in its after-hours release, while Alphabet's sales and profit missed estimates. Their shares diverged in extended trading. Oracle's longer-term cash-flow forecast had already helped regular-session sentiment. The combination gave investors neither a uniform rejection of AI spending nor a uniform demonstration that every large spending program was generating the expected return.

At 5:50 p.m. New York time, after the fixed-income close, Bloomberg reported a concrete delay in distributing a Texas data-center financing. Banks led by Morgan Stanley had hoped to sell $5 billion-$7 billion of high-yield bonds in September to refinance part of a roughly $15 billion construction package for the Nexus project in Hubbard, leased to Anthropic and backed by Google. Texas's moratorium on new projects pending a power-grid review has delayed the offering; sales may now be staggered over the next year.

The package included a $14.2 billion one-year loan and a $1.4 billion five-year revolving facility. The bridge loan has been funded, leaving lenders with disbursed exposure rather than only an undrawn promise. Citi, Intesa Sanpaolo, Mizuho, Morgan Stanley, MUFG, Royal Bank of Canada and Santander arranged it, with roughly $2 billion committed by each bank. Some lenders, including Santander, were seeking additional participants. The postponement extends the period for which the banks carry the risk and makes the state review consequential for their intended refinancing timetable.

## Borrower Stress Reaches Prices and Creditor Terms

Dave & Buster's hired Moelis to help address $1.5 billion of debt, while a creditor group working with PJT Partners and Gibson Dunn executed a cooperation pact and sought more signatures. The agreement aims to broaden coordination among lenders at a time when restructurings can divide creditors into competing groups. No restructuring terms were announced.

The arcade operator's $691 million term loan due in 2029 was quoted at 55.875 cents Wednesday, down from 93.75 cents on February 17. Its debt consists of term loans and a revolving facility. Second-quarter same-store sales fell 2.9% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings declined to $98.9 million from $129.8 million. Moody's retained the B3 corporate rating in September but changed the outlook to negative, citing weak interest coverage, high leverage and sluggish performance. The adviser appointment adds a new response to that deterioration.

Aston Martin's quarterly results showed operating improvement insufficient to prevent a further increase in debt. Its Q3 pretax loss narrowed to £77 million, revenue rose 36% to £389 million as sales shifted toward more expensive vehicles, and management maintained guidance while reporting progress on cash burn. Net debt nonetheless rose to £1.57 billion. Its bonds traded around 47 cents Wednesday, compared with about 55 cents at the start of October.

That position has weighed on Arini Capital Management, whose flagship fund lost 12% in October through October 23 and around 26% for the year. The flagship had $7.5 billion under management at July's end. People familiar with its trading said founder Hamza Lemssouguer was managing existing positions more defensively and bidding less actively for additional debt. Other investors were also becoming reluctant to buy weaker credits in which Arini held large stakes.

The feedback is visible in individual securities. Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection's $300 million bond due in 2028 fell below 75 cents from more than 92 at September's end. A Bloomberg index of European CCC debt had already lost money for four consecutive months through September, and October was shaping up as its worst month in four years. Sona Asset Management's main hedge fund was separately down 3.1% in the first half of October. Those losses have reduced the willingness of some traditional buyers to act as a counterweight in the weakest debt.

Arini is also receiving new capital. It raised $1.5 billion for its credit strategy and reopened to existing investors, with more than $400 million allocated at October's start and the remainder due to be deployed through February. That timetable distinguishes a less aggressive current bid from an absence of incoming funds. Its Aston Martin exposure also sits beside creditor litigation over the carmaker's earlier £550 million HPS financing; the new quarterly results and bond prices, rather than a new resolution of that dispute, were Wednesday's developments.

Trans-Oil suffered a sharper immediate price response to a disclosure delay. Its $450 million November 2029 bond fell as much as 7.4 cents to 58 after the Moldovan grain exporter said audited results for the year ended June 30 would be published by November 27 at the latest. The company attributed the additional time to completing audit procedures. It plans to publish first-quarter operating results on October 30 and described its estimates as encouraging despite difficult logistics and regional supply concerns. July commitments of more than $245 million and an extension of its borrowing-base facility remain distinct from the refinancing and upsizing it had planned for this month.

Research on loan documentation provided a broader explanation for creditors' attention to legal protections. JPMorgan data cited Wednesday put the share of U.S. leveraged loans trading above par at 9.8%, a 17-month low. A new Barclays study by Corry Short found that stronger creditor documentation could improve new-issue pricing, while questioning how much independent importance should be assigned to an aggressive sponsor's reputation. The distinction matters when weak covenants allow liability-management transactions to change recoveries among lenders even before the business's ultimate debt-paying capacity is settled.

Small trucking operators supplied a separate, newly reported measure of financial pressure. Bloomberg counted 221 trucking-company bankruptcies this year. A Truckstop and Bloomberg Intelligence survey conducted over the past two months found about two-thirds of small carriers reporting flat or lower revenue from a year earlier; almost 40% expected to have left trucking in six months or were unsure of their future. These were firms generally operating 20 or fewer tractors, not findings about the largest listed carriers.

Their vulnerability combines diesel and insurance bills with equipment debt, variable-rate borrowing, factoring and merchant cash advances. Stoneman Trucking, which entered bankruptcy protection in May, is moving toward Chapter 7 liquidation after its owner abandoned hopes of continuing. Larger operators with less equipment debt can absorb costs more readily; Triumph Financial's Aaron Graft said firms with no equipment debt and qualified safety records were doing well. The survey thus identifies a particular borrower cohort under pressure rather than a common financial state across freight companies.

Funding alternatives remain available to some businesses. Lionsgate is discussing a possible library-backed bond transaction with investors through MUFG. Its catalog contains more than 20,000 films and television shows and generates about $1 billion annually, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. The studio had more than $1.9 billion of corporate debt on June 30, including an intellectual-property-linked loan exceeding $1 billion due in September 2030, at 225 basis points over SOFR and quarterly principal repayments of 2.5% of the then-outstanding balance. Securitization could lower funding costs, BI's Geetha Ranganathan said, while reducing flexibility to use the catalog in a potential takeover. Discussions remain preliminary, with no offering terms established.

## Sovereign Funding Depends on the Buyer and Maturity

A new analysis of Treasury and State Department data showed a substantial change in the source of U.S. financing over the first eight months of 2026. Countries and regions classified as most aligned with Washington bought a net $174.3 billion of Treasuries excluding bills, more than 60% below a year earlier and the lowest corresponding total since 2021. Japan bought only $389 million, down 99%, while South Korea sold $23.8 billion, the most for that period in records beginning in 1977. Taiwan was also a net seller.

The analysis covers official and private investors in 57 countries and regions, using voting alignment on key United Nations resolutions to define the groups. Purchases concern securities originally issued with maturities above one year. Custodial attribution can assign holdings to financial centers rather than ultimate owners. The figures establish a change in recorded demand, not a single government-directed policy of selling U.S. debt.

Weak Asian currencies, more attractive home-market yields and a greater preference for equities and deposits offer different explanations for the shift. Council on Foreign Relations fellow Brad Setser described foreign assets increasingly residing outside central-bank reserves, including at pension funds and state banks. That can reduce official Treasury demand while leaving substantial demand for dollar assets elsewhere.

Foreign holdings were still $7.85 trillion in August, near a record, even as their share fell below a third from 52% in 2012. Private investors including banks, mutual funds and hedge funds had increased their share of federal debt to about 70%, near the highest since 1990. The implication drawn by State Street's Masahiko Loo and Deutsche Bank's Shoki Omori was greater dependence on price-sensitive buyers. This is a structural financing finding about January-August, not a measurement of Wednesday's flows.

Britain demonstrated the immediate value of changing the maturity mix. Gilts rose after Chancellor John Healey's budget and a Debt Management Office reduction in planned longer-maturity supply to £15.5 billion from £22.4 billion. The DMO increased reliance on bills and confirmed that 12-month bills would be offered by tender from January 2027. Ten-year gilt yields fell as much as 4 basis points to 5.30% during the response.

The Office for Budget Responsibility confirmed £15 billion of fiscal headroom in 2029-30. Investors welcomed the absence of major long-term giveaways and a debt-to-GDP profile that remained broadly flat while the deficit declined. By 3 p.m. London time, the 10-year yield had moved through a range of only 7 basis points, compared with 22 on Rachel Reeves' first budget day in 2024 and 40 during the 2022 mini-budget. The realized borrowing plan supplied the concrete terms behind the earlier expectation of less long-dated issuance.

China faces a different combination of heavy supply and low yields. China Chengxin International Credit Rating and Industrial Securities estimate at least 2.2 trillion yuan of net central- and local-government bond sales in November and December, the second-largest total for those months after 2024. Net financing had reached 11.15 trillion yuan through October 23. The 10-year yield was around 1.62%, near a record low, while the PBOC added liquidity on a net basis for a sixth consecutive session Wednesday.

The prospective sales are intended to support activity amid weak consumption, employment and infrastructure investment. Yuan Haixia at China Chengxin expects stronger fiscal support to narrow the infrastructure contraction, while anticipating open-market operations to smooth issuance-related liquidity fluctuations. Industrial Securities sees November as a possible supply peak but warns actual issuance may depart materially from plans as policy and economic conditions change. The forecast financing remains distinct from funds already spent.

In Japan, new manager interviews showed a more constructive sovereign-duration stance. T. Rowe Price favors longer debt, Allianz Global Investors is selectively adding intermediate and long maturities, and BNP Paribas Asset Management has increased exposure to 20- and 30-year bonds. The 30-year yield had fallen almost 40 basis points from its 4.25% peak earlier in October, and the two- to 30-year gap had narrowed about 70 basis points since July. Life insurers had bought super-long JGBs on a net basis for four months, and foreign investors for three.

These buyers see recovering demand and further BOJ tightening as potentially supporting a smaller term premium. Their confidence remains conditional on fiscal funding. Brandywine's Carol Lye has not restored the 30-year holdings sold earlier this year, citing the need for a credible plan. T. Rowe Price's Vincent Chung and Deutsche Securities' Omori likewise warned that unfunded spending or an issuance plan failing to reduce super-long supply could reverse the flattening.

Japanese corporate credit is moving differently. Reporting published after the U.S. close showed five-year CDS rising on all 40 major Japanese companies tracked by Bloomberg between October 1 and October 28, with a median increase of 12 basis points, the largest deterioration since September 2022. SoftBank and Nissan led the widening. Domestic corporate spreads were around a two-and-a-half-year high. Nomura's Kazuma Ogino linked the pressure to heavy supply and lower government yields, alongside concerns about AI investment and French public finances. The recovery in sovereign demand has not translated into equally favorable pricing for corporate borrowers.

## Central Banks Split on Energy Pass-Through

Canada raised its overnight rate to 2.5%, its first increase in more than three years, to reduce the risk that sustained high energy prices broaden into other goods and services. The move was expected by markets and the Bloomberg economist consensus. Governor Tiff Macklem said further tightening could be necessary but that uncertainty warranted proceeding carefully, one meeting at a time.

The forecast revision was substantial. Average inflation in 2027 is now projected at 3.1%, against 2% previously, with a return to the 2% target delayed until mid-2028. Growth forecasts rose to 1% for 2026 from 0.7%, and to 2% for both 2027 and 2028 from 1.8%. Macklem said current energy pass-through was limited but expected non-energy inflation to rise next year as costs propagated through the economy.

The council also considered holding. Energy still accounted for much of the inflation increase, economic slack remained and the U.S. tariff dispute threatened growth. Employment had declined for two months and housing was weak. The Canadian dollar was little changed around C$1.4046 per U.S. dollar after the announcement, while two-year yields edged lower within the session's range. The expected rate increase did not produce an equally forceful market repricing.

Housing exposes the domestic cost of acting against an imported shock. The bank now projects residential real estate contributing virtually nothing to growth through 2028. Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said higher rates would add to existing restraint. Desjardins analysts Royce Mendes and Tiago Figueiredo estimated roughly 50% payment shocks for some variable-rate borrowers renewing in coming months, while noting mortgage arrears remained below historical levels. Frequent renewals and widespread variable-rate borrowing bring monetary restraint to households faster than long-fixed-rate structures do.

In a separate interview, Macklem argued that large U.S. deficits and AI borrowing could push up longer-term yields globally and potentially Canada's neutral rate. He did not revise the bank's 2.25%-3.25% neutral estimate, which is reviewed annually in April. He also rejected the suggestion that the new Prima forecasting model itself caused Wednesday's hike. The model integrates costs across sectors; the policy concern remains the future path of total inflation.

New Zealand chose to wait despite a pronounced inflation risk. The RBNZ held the Official Cash Rate at 2.75% by 4-3, surprising 23 of 25 economists who expected a quarter-point increase. Paul Conway, Hayley Gourley and Karen Silk voted to raise. Governor Anna Breman and member Prasanna Gai, among the hold majority, attached material weight to the possibility of an abrupt global shift affecting demand.

The committee said tighter policy was likely to be needed, conditional on the outlook. Q3 inflation had eased to 3.7%, but the bank expected 4.4% in Q4 as fuel costs and a weaker currency lifted prices. Economists expected inflation above the 1%-3% band until late 2027. Subdued household spending was limiting some firms' ability to pass on costs, while prolonged inflation risked influencing expectations and wage setting. The New Zealand dollar fell as much as 1.7% to 55.86 U.S. cents immediately after the surprise hold.

Thailand maintained its 1% repurchase rate for a fourth meeting, with all six attending committee members in favor and the seventh absent. The bank raised growth forecasts to 2.4% this year and 2.1% in 2027 from 2.3% and 1.8%, citing AI-related exports and investment. It lowered core-inflation forecasts to 1.2% and 1.3% from 1.5% and 1.4%. September exports had risen 24% annually, but tourism, heavily indebted households and fragile labor conditions limited the breadth of the improvement.

Assistant Governor Don Nakornthab said a continued recovery would permit less accommodation and rebuilding policy space, while leaving room to cut after an economic shock. The statement warned of financial-stability consequences from keeping rates low for too long. Pantheon Macroeconomics' Miguel Chanco read the tone as neutral rather than the August meeting's dovish stance. Economists remained divided between eventual normalization and renewed easing, reflecting a much less uniform demand recovery than in the U.S.

Australia's prospective decision drew a fresh forecast change rather than a realized hike. Commonwealth Bank economist Belinda Allen now expects the RBA to raise rates to 4.85% in November. She cited excessive September-quarter inflation, more hawkish official communication and the interaction of weak productivity with strong global capital expenditure. Her proposed insurance increase would address upside risks from offshore energy costs and domestic capacity pressure, illustrating another point on the spectrum between Canada's immediate action and New Zealand's surprise patience.

## Forward Market Significance

Thursday's U.S. growth and inflation releases at 12:30 UTC will supply the first major data test after the Fed's pause. Q3 GDP consensus is 3.2% annualized, against 2.2% previously, while the Atlanta Fed's latest model estimate is 3.3%. September core PCE is expected to increase 0.3% monthly and 3.1% annually, up from 0.2% and 3%. Headline PCE expectations are 0.5% on the month and 3.6% on the year, against 0.3% and 3.4%. Those combinations will help determine whether the market can sustain a smaller projected tightening cycle while officials continue to describe growth as strong.

The same release time brings personal spending, expected to rise 0.6% after 0.9%, and income, expected up 0.3% after 0.2%. Initial claims consensus is 199,000 for the week ended October 24, compared with 194,000 previously; continuing claims are expected at 1.720 million against 1.728 million. The Q3 GDP price index is expected to slow to 3.2% from 6.1%, and quarterly core PCE prices to 2.4% from 3.3%. The quarterly price measures describe a different period from September's monthly readings, allowing the releases to show deceleration over the quarter alongside a firmer final month.

Japan's two-year auction Thursday and BOJ decision Friday will test the returning demand for government debt. Officials are widely expected to hold rates at this meeting, leaving Governor Kazuo Ueda's guidance on subsequent tightening and the eventual policy peak important for longer maturities. The larger condition for the new long-end buyers is a credible fiscal 2027 funding plan, including how proposed food-tax relief and defense spending will be financed. A supply plan that disappoints their expectations could interrupt the recent curve flattening.

U.S. midterm ballots contain at least $84 billion of state and local bond proposals, above roughly $81 billion in 2024 and $16 billion last year in Bloomberg's comparison of large referendums. California accounts for roughly $60 billion and Texas about $10 billion. California's largest measures seek $25 billion of revenue bonds for home-buying assistance and $11.25 billion of general-obligation debt for affordable housing. These are requests for voter authorization, not a completed issuance calendar; the outcome will shape a potential financing pipeline for housing and infrastructure.

For AI credit, the Texas power-grid review now governs the delayed Hubbard bond takeout, while Barclays' insurance discussions depend on counterparties accepting additional exposure. Those separate unresolved conditions bear directly on how quickly banks can recycle capital. In public markets, the divergence between Microsoft and Alphabet puts fresh operating results beside the continuing financing requirement, rather than leaving demand for computing capacity as a single sector-wide assumption.

Trans-Oil's October 30 operating release and November 27 latest date for audited annual statements are near-term disclosure tests after its bond selloff. They address different reporting periods and will allow creditors to assess the company's recovery claims and financial position. For U.S. leisure credit, Six Flags' November 5 results will provide management's next update after safety incidents and depressed bond prices; CBRE's Colin Mansfield argues that season-pass information early next year will be needed for a fairer assessment of the operating trajectory.

The energy outlook remains dependent on military and diplomatic decisions as well as inventories. The reported prospect of renewed U.S. attacks after the November 3 vote leaves the duration of the fuel shock unsettled. Bessent expects well-supplied oil markets once the conflict is resolved and has urged an open mind about transitory inflation; Canada's new forecast instead assumes enough persistence to generate broader price effects next year. The path of the conflict will help determine which of those conditions develops, with direct consequences for the inflation compensation that rose in Wednesday's Treasury market.

overall_summary.headline: Fed pause supports short Treasuries as higher inflation compensation lifts long yields
overall_summary.session_narrative:
The Fed held its target range at 3.75%-4% by 10-2, with both dissenters seeking a quarter-point increase. Kevin Warsh acknowledged tighter financial conditions without calling them tight and left the next move open. Investors trimmed expectations for subsequent tightening rather than abandoning December: post-decision futures pricing still put a quarter-point increase around 90%.

The 2-year Treasury yield fell 3.94 basis points to 4.6975%, while the 10-year rose 2.08 basis points to 5.0175% and the 30-year increased 3.23 basis points to 5.3426%. The 2- to 10-year spread widened 6.02 basis points to 32 basis points. At 10 years, a 3.09-basis-point rise in inflation compensation more than offset a 1.01-basis-point decline in real yields. Higher oil prices reinforced concern about persistent energy pressure.

Credit restraint remained selective. Barclays was exploring insurance on more than $10 billion of AI infrastructure debt to make room for further lending, while at least 18 data-center financings carried double-digit yields. U.S. high-yield spreads were little changed and hard-currency EM spreads tightened noticeably. Thursday's GDP and PCE releases will test whether strong growth and inflation allow the market's smaller projected tightening cycle to hold.
